account: It is six in the morning on day 1, and I have just woken at home. I have not yet seen anyone or learned any news today. Nothing I personally observed yesterday suggested an unusual disturbance. The baker was reported carrying wheat and was busy preparing fresh bread for market; that appears consistent with ordinary bakery work, not evidence of anything improper. My neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage described a quiet afternoon and had no pressing concerns. I kept our tea appointment and was invited back today at three. The secretary reported no new correspondence yesterday and secured the appointment book in its chest. At my request, the secretary planned to confirm today's ten o'clock mill grain inspection and ask for existing stock and delivery records, shortages, and storage concerns. Those requests are preparation for routine town business; I have not yet received confirmation or learned of any actual grain shortage. I should go to the office, read today's appointment book, and meet the secretary at eight. The schedule I previously read also lists lunch at home at noon, council letters at one, tea at three, office at half past four, and home at seven.
